title: Classes where “other pay” is more than a fifth of salary
question: In which job classes do payments outside regular salary and overtime come to more than a fifth of salary, and is that routine or recent?
finding: This is uncommon. Across the City, pay recorded as “other” was 5.8% of regular salary in fiscal 2026 ($282.5 million). Only 13 job classes with five or more holders were above a fifth that year, and 1 of those had been above it routinely (in eight of the ten years, or in every year the class had five holders): Director (class 1115), Retirement System (53.1%). The largest in money is Sergeant 3 (class Q052): $18.3 million for 412 holders, 23.0% of salary, up from 8.0% in fiscal 2017. 5 of the 13 classes were under a tenth when first counted.
how: City payroll file, fiscal 2017 to 2026. The file describes “other salaries” as irregular payments including premium pay, incentive pay and one-time payments. For each class and fiscal year, other pay is added up across everyone paid regular salary in the class and divided by their regular salary; only years in which the class had five or more holders are counted. Listed: classes over 20% in fiscal 2026, with the number of counted years over 20% and the share in the first counted year. Board seats, elected offices and the Superior Court are left out. Ranked by years over a fifth, then by money.
limits: The file’s own description names premium pay, incentive pay and one-time payments. A share that rose only in the last few years may follow a new agreement. The figure shows where pay sits outside the published salary scale, not that any payment was improper; the pay codes behind “other”, which the public file does not carry, would show what each payment was for.
